design.md's `## ADR Change Log` (lines 269-305) references ADR-0017, 0018, 0020, 0021, 0022, all confirmed present at docs/adr/ (verified by directory listing). However, this same section names two mechanisms the spec's own text repeatedly calls its 'own proposal, not found verbatim in decision v2 or an ADR' — the Registry discovery contract (REQ-005: script-relative -> git-root -> fail-closed, per-artifact version check, release-gating vendored-copy drift check) and the Gate implementation identity mechanism (REQ-003(c)) — and states 'No new ADR is proposed by this spec' for either. The round-2 edit adds a rationale (both single-Epic-scoped today; promotion deferred until a second real consumer, e.g. Epic A5, adopts the pattern) and a matching Risks entry, but design.md's own Cross-Layer Dependencies (lines 262-267) and Risks (lines 1113-1127) already name Epic A5's Resolver as a specific, anticipated future consumer of the identical discovery pattern, and the Risks entry itself states the unmitigated consequence plainly: 'if Epic A5 instead designs its own, materially different discovery convention, the two Epics would carry two undocumented, divergent patterns for the same problem with no ADR recording either as canonical.' This is precisely the architectural-departure-with-no-ADR condition this check flags — a self-acknowledged, concrete implementation-misalignment risk, not a hypothetical one. This repository's own convention formalizes comparable cross-cutting/reusable mechanisms as ADRs (e.g. ADR-0011 backs the human-copy protected-file pattern this same spec itself reuses, docs/adr/0011-phase2-handle-relative-protected-copy.md), which weighs against treating a deliberately-reusable discovery contract as adequately covered by an unpromoted, single-document design decision. The Gate implementation identity mechanism is comparatively more defensible as a non-ADR decision since no other Epic is named as a consumer of that specific mechanism (its scan-root literal is scoped only to this Epic's own validator), but the Registry discovery contract's named cross-Epic exposure is not resolved by the added rationale alone. Recommend: either author a lightweight ADR now for the Registry discovery contract, or have Epic A5's own spec explicitly commit to adopting it verbatim before Epic A5's design is approved, so the 'two divergent patterns' risk design.md's own Risks section names does not remain open indefinitely.
